summary.text: Cyndi Munson, a Democrat who has represented Oklahoma House District 85 since 2015, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Governor of Oklahoma to Mike Mazzei.
She served as House Minority Leader from 2022 to 2026 and was the first Asian American woman elected to the Oklahoma Legislature.

paragraphs.text: Munson was born in Monterey, California, and raised in Lawton, Oklahoma.

She was the first in her family to earn a college degree, receiving a B.A. in political science from the University of Central Oklahoma through the Oklahoma's Promise tuition program and later a master's degree in leadership education from the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.
Before entering politics she worked in the nonprofit sector, including at the OK Messages Project and Girl Scouts of Western Oklahoma.
She lost her first House race, in 2014, to the incumbent, then won a 2015 special election for House District 85 with more than 54% of the vote.
In 2019 she was selected for the oversight committee of the Legislative Office for Fiscal Transparency.
Munson succeeded Emily Virgin as House Minority Leader in 2022 and left the House as Minority Leader after the 2026 legislative session, not seeking re-election to her seat.
She announced her campaign for governor in April 2025 as the first Democrat in the race and won the June 16, 2026 Democratic primary with about 74.9% of the vote.
During the campaign, she emphasized more funding for public schools, repealing the parental choice tax credit, a state question to overturn the abortion ban and a moratorium on new data centers.
She received 45.9% of the vote to Mike Mazzei's 51.9%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
